### Summary

Output block `<n>` of the card (counting from 0) is stream `out<n>`. Block `<r>` writes frame `<kkkkk>` of that
stream to `<basename>.block<r>.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc`. The combined file is `<basename>.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc`. Every rank returns
from the write only after the combined file exists.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Writes each block's part of an output frame to its own NetCDF-4 file, then joins them into one.

**Data.** Reads the selected variables of the block; writes `<basename>.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc`.

**Placement.** `make_outputs` after an accepted step; the root joins the parts with the in-tree `combine_parts`.

**Activation.** `outputs: - type: netcdf` with `dt`, `variables`[^rg-9edf1a86e51f] and options; CMake `NETCDF` (default ON).

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact copy, then float32 unless `double_precision`[^rg-60f001cddf89]: at most $2^{-24}$ relative.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch14-netcdf-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $f$ a cubed-sphere panel, $0..5$ [count]; $n_{b2}$, $n_{b3}$ the
blocks per panel along $x_2$, $x_3$ [count]; $\mathrm{fl}_{32}(x)$ the float32 value nearest a double $x$; $t$ the
written time [s].

Units of the output fields: a variable carries a `units` attribute where the metadata table sets one, in SI[^rg-8c117ccbf00d]: `rho`
kg/m^3, `press` Pa, `vel1..3` m/s, `temp` and `theta` K, the vertical coordinate m and `time` s; `dens`, `Etot`,
`mom1..3` and the species fields carry none (@tbl-ch14-netcdf-contract-4, @tbl-ch14-netcdf-contract-5,
@tbl-ch14-netcdf-contract-6).

Primitive and conserved variables, in the deck and in the output. The conserved variables are the rows of
`hydro_u` that the scheme advances: row 0 the dry density (the total density under `ideal-gas`), rows 1-3 the
momenta, row 4 the total energy and rows 5 onward the partial densities of the species (O-16, O-17). The primitive
variables are the rows of `hydro_w` at the same indices: total density, velocities, pressure and mass fractions.
In the deck, the `variables:` list of an output stream chooses which set is written: `prim` writes the primitive
variables as `rho`, `press`, `vel1 vel2 vel3` (O-18), and `cons` writes the conserved ones as `dens`, `Etot`,
`mom1 mom2 mom3` (O-19).

Reading a file in Python: open the combined file with `xarray` (or `netCDF4`); a cell-centred field has dimensions
`(time, x1, x3, x2)` with $x_1$ the vertical (O-29). Temperature is `temp`, written by the `thermo` keyword (O-24)
and by the user output of the Straka example:

```python
import xarray as xr
ds = xr.open_dataset("straka_single.out0.00001.nc")  # <basename>.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc
T = ds["temp"].isel(time=0, x3=0)                    # one x2-x1 slice, units K
T.plot(x="x2", y="x1")                               # needs matplotlib
```

### Derivation

The output copies values and, by default, rounds them to float32. What that rounding costs, in four steps:

1. *The conversion.* Unless `double_precision: true`, each value is converted with `t.to(torch::kFloat32)` before
   `nc_put_vara_float`, so snapy narrows and NetCDF does not ({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp Values >}}). The cast
   rounds to nearest.
2. *Relative error.* For $\lvert x\rvert$ in the float32 normal range $[2^{-126},\,(2-2^{-23})\,2^{127}]$, rounding to the
   nearest of 24 significant bits gives $\lvert\mathrm{fl}_{32}(x)-x\rvert\le 2^{-24}\lvert x\rvert\approx5.96\times10^{-8}\lvert x\rvert$.
3. *Outside that range.* A value above $\approx3.40\times10^{38}$ becomes infinite, and stays so in the file, because
   the narrowing is snapy's, not NetCDF's (which would store the float fill value). One below $2^{-126}$ goes
   subnormal, with absolute error at most $2^{-150}$.
4. *The time.* The time is written in the same type. Near $t$ the float32 spacing lies between $2^{-24}t$ and
   $2^{-23}t$, so a step shorter than $2^{-25}t$ always vanishes from the written time and one longer than
   $2^{-23}t$ always shows. This is the "time step below ~1e-7 * t" of the code comment.

With `double_precision: true` the file holds the doubles exactly. `[C17]`–`[C19]` of `derivation_check.py` check
steps 2 to 4.

### Numerical method

**Options.** The keys of one stream are the rows of the options table `src/options/output.yaml`, read by the
generated `read_output_rows`; any other key is an error ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
The slice checks run when the card is read and again against the resolved global grid, through `check_domain`
({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputOptionsImpl::check_domain >}}), which the block calls for every output
when it builds them ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}).

**One block's file.** `GriddedWriter`, the writer of `netcdf` and `pnetcdf`, does nothing on the final write, so the
last frame of a run is the last scheduled one (@sec-ch14-schedule). It loads the selected fields, copies each to the
host as float64 once, sets the index range (the interior, or with `include_ghost_zones` the interior plus
$n_g$[^rg-88a9e0a977ff] ghosts on every axis with more than one cell), applies slices and sums, and hands the frame to
the NetCDF sink ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp GriddedWriter::write_output_file >}};
{{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp output_range >}}). A slice key holds a list of coordinates: each selects the cell
that contains it, with no interpolation, a list on several axes selects their Cartesian product, and a block that
contains none of them writes no part (`Frame::transform`, {{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp Frame::transform >}}).
The sink creates the file with `nc_create(..., NC_NETCDF4, ...)` ({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfSink::write >}}).
Each block records its position in the global block grid as the `domain_decomposition` attribute of each axis. For
the cubed sphere the six panels are laid out as a $3 \times 2$ tile: panel $f$ is shifted by $(f \bmod 3)\,n_{b2}$ in
$x_2$ and $\lfloor f/3 \rfloor\,n_{b3}$ in $x_3$, and the global counts become $3n_{b2}$ and $2n_{b3}$
(`output_block_location`, {{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp output_block_location >}}). Every variable, the time
included, is NC_FLOAT unless `double_precision: true`, which makes it NC_DOUBLE
({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfSink::write >}}).

**The combine.** `combine_on_root` counts the blocks of the process that have reached this frame. Only the last of
them goes on, so one thread per process enters the collective part. That thread waits at a barrier. It then
creates a scope guard whose destructor is a second barrier, so no rank returns before the root has finished, and a
throw on the root still releases the others ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp combine_on_root >}}). On the root,
`combine_netcdf_blocks` globs `<basename>.block*.out<n>.<kkkkk>.nc` and removes any old combined file. One part is
renamed; several parts are passed to `combine_parts`, which joins them and removes the parts
({{< code src/output/combine_netcdf.cpp combine_netcdf_blocks >}}). `combine_parts` is snapy's own joiner: it takes the
structure of the first part, places every split variable at the offset its `domain_decomposition` attribute gives,
requires one time record per part and refuses to overwrite an existing file
({{< code src/output/combine_parts.cpp combine_parts >}}).

With `combine: false` the per-block files stay. Joining them later needs an external joiner such as GFDL's
`mppnccombine`; `pd-combine` does not join blocks (@sec-ch14-tools).

#### What is in the file

**Which writers exist.**

A first-year reading: every entry of the `outputs:` list in the YAML card is one *stream*. Its `type:` picks the writer
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reset >}}).

| id | `type:` | what you get |
|---|---|---|
| O-1 | `netcdf` | one NetCDF-4 file per block per frame, joined into one file per frame (`GriddedWriter` with the NetCDF sink) |
| O-2 | `pnetcdf` | parallel-NetCDF writer (@sec-ch14-pnetcdf); needs the build option `PNETCDF=ON`, otherwise "Output type 'pnetcdf' requires PNETCDF[^rg-0346eddcaa68]=ON." |
| O-3 | `restart` | tensor dump of the block state, for resuming (@sec-ch14-restart) |
| O-3b | `budget` | the budget time series of the flux register (@sec-ch13) |
| O-4 | anything else (`hdf5`, `fits`, …) | refused: "Output type '…' is not implemented." |
| O-5 | (no `type:`) | refused: "OutputOptions::from_yaml: output file type must be specified" |

**The YAML keys of one stream, and the cadence.**

| id | key (default) | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| O-6 | the accepted keys | `dt`, `output_sumx1`, `output_sumx2`, `output_sumx3`, `include_ghost_zones`, `double_precision`, `x1_slice`, `x2_slice`, `x3_slice`, `type`[^rg-ddd3dfc3359d], `variables`, `combine`, `verbose`: the rows of `src/options/output.yaml`. Any other key is an error |
| O-7 | `dt` (0.) | output interval in simulation seconds |
| O-8 | `double_precision` (false) | NetCDF variables are `NC_FLOAT` unless this is true. `pnetcdf` refuses `true` (@sec-ch14-pnetcdf) |
| O-9 | `combine` (true) | join the per-block parts after each write |
| O-11 | stream number | streams are numbered from 0 in card order, and stream *n* is named `out<n>` ({{< code src/output/output_type.hpp OutputOptionsImpl::file_id >}}) |

: Netcdf contract, table 2. {#tbl-ch14-netcdf-contract-2}

**Inside a NetCDF file: names, units, prognostic or diagnostic.**

Two state arrays sit behind the names:

- `hydro_w` is the *primitive* state: total density $\rho$[^rg-bc477a8d0f7b], velocities, pressure, and mass fractions $y$.
- `hydro_u` is the *conserved* (prognostic) state: dry density (for `ideal-moist`), partial densities $\rho y$, momenta, total energy.

| id | fact | source |
|---|---|---|
| O-16 | Row order of both arrays in the default build (`NMASS` = 0): 0 density, 1-3 velocity or momentum, 4 pressure or energy, 5 onward species | `NMASS` in `cmake/parameters.cmake`, the index enum of {{< code src/snap.h >}} |
| O-17 | In `hydro_u`, row 0 is the **dry** density $(1-\sum y)\rho$ and the species rows are partial densities $y\rho$; in `hydro_w`, row 0 is the **total** density $\rho$ and the species rows are mass fractions $y$ (`ideal-moist`) | @sec-ch02 |

| id | keyword | NetCDF variable names; `units` attribute | from; kind | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Watch-outs for a reader of the files:

- Mass fractions, partial densities, `dens`, `Etot` and `mom*` carry no `units` attribute at all (O-18, O-19). Their
  SI units are not stated in any output code.
- **Hypothesis, not run:** `variables: [prim, cons]` on a deck with species defines each species name twice: once
  from `hydro_w`, once from `hydro_u` (O-18, O-19), and the second `nc_def_var` of a name would fail.

**Dimensions, coordinates and ghost cells in NetCDF.**

| id | fact | source |
|---|---|---|
| O-29 | A cell-centred 3-D field has dimensions **`(time, x1, x3, x2)`**: x1 (vertical) comes first and x2 comes last. Face fields swap in `x1f`, `x2f` or `x3f` at the same slot | {{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp field_dims >}} |
| O-30 | `time` is unlimited, but each file holds **one** time record. A run gives one file per frame | {{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfSink::write >}} |
| O-33 | The coordinate variables carry axis labels `x1`[^rg-9792da14d102] "Z", `x2` "X" and `x3` "Y", with long names "<axis>-coordinate at cell center" and "…at cell face". `x1` has units "m"; `x2` and `x3` have "radian" on `gnomonic-equiangle` and `spherical-polar` grids and "m" otherwise | {{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp axis_text >}}; {{< code src/output/output_utils.hpp horizontal_axis_units >}} |
| O-34 | On `gnomonic-equiangle`, the written `x2` and `x3` of a panel are shifted by $\tfrac\pi2$ times its column and row in the $3\times2$ layout, so the panels' angles follow one another along each joined axis | {{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfSink::write >}} |
| O-36 | Part names concatenate `<basename>`, `.block<r>`, `.out<n>` and `.<kkkkk>.nc`; joined names omit `.block<r>`. The global attribute `NumFilesInSet` holds the number of blocks that write a part: every block, or with slice lists the blocks whose cells contain a listed coordinate on each sliced axis, times six on the cubed sphere | {{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfSink::write >}}; {{< code src/output/combine_netcdf.cpp combine_netcdf_blocks >}} |

: Netcdf contract, table 6. {#tbl-ch14-netcdf-contract-6}

Cadence is described in @sec-ch14-schedule. The existing ghost-zone limits above still apply.

### Add a new output field {#sec-ch14-add-output-field}

A field is a named tensor loaded into an existing output stream. `OutputType::LoadOutputData` calls the hydro,
diagnostic, scalar and user loaders in that order
({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::LoadOutputData >}}).
Keep `type: netcdf` in `outputs`[^rg-b5340f5bdc7f] for a snapshot of a new diagnostic; `type` selects the writer, while `variables` selects fields.
The procedure below adds a cell-centred scalar without adding a writer.

1. **Choose the loader.** For a case-specific field, register `MeshBlockImpl::user_output_callback` on each block
   before its first output, following {{< code examples/run_hydro.cpp main >}}. Return a map from a nonempty field
   name to a tensor; select `variables: [uov]` (or `[user_out_var]`) to write all entries.
   `OutputType::loadUserOutputData` refuses a missing callback and appends each entry as one field
   ({{< code src/output/load_user_output_data.cpp OutputType::loadUserOutputData >}}).
   For a built-in diagnostic, edit `OutputType::loadDiagOutputData` in
   {{< code src/output/load_diag_output_data.cpp OutputType::loadDiagOutputData >}};
   state fields instead belong in `OutputType::loadHydroOutputData`
   ({{< code src/output/load_hydro_output_data.cpp OutputType::loadHydroOutputData >}}).
2. **Register the selection and data.** There is no separate field registry: `OutputType::ContainVariable`
   matches strings in the stream's options
   ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::ContainVariable >}}).
   Add a guarded append in the loader. For example, this proposed addition copies the existing total-density
   field under a new name; replace its tensor expression with the intended diagnostic:

   ```cpp
   if (ContainVariable("rho_copy")) {
     auto const& w = vars.at("hydro_w");
     appendTensorOutput("rho_copy", w[IDN]);
   }
   ```

   Place this branch directly in the loader body, outside the other keyword guards. Retain the full cell array,
   including its ghosts, as the existing loaders do. `OutputType::appendTensorOutput` accepts a tensor of one to three
   dimensions and adds it to the frame as one field
   ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputType::appendTensorOutput >}}).
3. **Add metadata and rebuild.** Add `{"rho_copy", "copy of total density", "kg/m^3", "CCC"}` to the table in
   `MetadataTable::MetadataTable` ({{< code src/output/output_utils.cpp MetadataTable::MetadataTable >}}).
   The columns are name, long name, units and grid location. The NetCDF sink takes the attributes from that table by
   field name; an unknown name gets no units or long name, and its grid location defaults to cells
   ({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfSink::write >}}).
4. **Select and locate it.** After rebuilding the source change, add this stream to the input deck:

   ```yaml
   outputs:
     - type: netcdf
       variables: [rho_copy]
       dt: 100.
   ```

   `OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml` copies the list into `options->variables()`
   ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
   As the first stream, it writes `rho_copy(time, x1, x3, x2)` in
   `<basename>.out0.<kkkkk>.nc`; with `combine: false`, use `<basename>.block<r>.out0.<kkkkk>.nc`.
   The sink defines the variable and `combine_netcdf_blocks` joins the block files
   ({{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfSink::write >}};
   {{< code src/output/combine_netcdf.cpp combine_netcdf_blocks >}}).
   Choosing `[rho_copy]` before adding its loader branch silently selects no such field.

For a new field, check its values, shape, name and units in a written file against the defining calculation.
The existing `UserOutput.registered_callback_allows_uov_output` and
`UserOutput.missing_callback_reports_meaningful_error` tests cover callback acceptance and refusal, not this proposed
field ({{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp UserOutput.registered_callback_allows_uov_output >}};
{{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp UserOutput.missing_callback_reports_meaningful_error >}}).

### Code

**A minimal input.** One NetCDF stream of the primitives and two diagnostics every 100 s, in double precision:

```yaml
outputs:
  - type: netcdf
    variables: [prim, uov]
    dt: 100.            # s; 0 writes every cycle
    double_precision: true
```

**What is refused, and why.** `MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml` reads the `outputs` list one entry at a time
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}), and `OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
parses each entry ({{< code src/output/output_type.cpp OutputOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}). In order:

1. *An unknown key* in the entry is an error, so a misspelt option, or one this pin does not have
   (`cartesian_vector`, `data_format`, `super-resolution`), is not silently dropped.
2. *A slice and a sum along the same axis* ("Cannot request both slice and sum along x1") is an error. One axis
   cannot be both cut and summed.
3. *A missing `type`* is an error ("output file type must be specified"). There is no default writer.
4. *A slice outside the mesh* is an error ("Slice out of mesh bounds: x1"), checked against the global
   lower-inclusive, upper-exclusive bounds, and so is *a slice list that is not strictly increasing* ("Slices must be
   strictly increasing: x1"), both checked by `check_domain` when the block builds its outputs. A slice is a YAML
   list, even for one coordinate (`x1_slice: [1.25]`); a scalar value fails to parse.
5. *An unknown `type`* is an error when the block builds its outputs ("Output type '…' is not implemented"); `pnetcdf`
   without `PNETCDF=ON` is refused there too.

**The excerpt.** The precision switch of step 1, in the NetCDF sink:

```cpp
    if (dbl)
      t = t.contiguous();
    else
      t = t.to(torch::kFloat32).contiguous();
```

| stream name | {{< code src/output/output_type.hpp OutputOptionsImpl::file_id >}} | `file_id` | none |
| one write of a gridded stream | {{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp GriddedWriter::write_output_file >}} | `GriddedWriter` | `type` |
| slices and sums | {{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp Frame::transform >}} | `transform` | `x*_slice`, `output_sumx*` |
| one block's file | {{< code src/output/netcdf.cpp NetcdfSink::write >}} | `NetcdfSink::write` | `include_ghost_zones` |

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_user_output` `OutputPrecision` (double) | values written with `double_precision` read back bit for bit | exact | NC_DOUBLE |
| `test_user_output` `OutputPrecision` (non-finite) | a non-finite value (an infinity) survives the float output | exact class | IEEE |
| `test_user_output` `OutputPrecision` (default, no NetCDF) | default off and reported by the options printout; a build without NetCDF writes nothing | exact | string compare |
| `test_user_output` `OutputSlice.*`, `OutputSelection.*`, `OutputDiagnostics.*`, `OutputStatistics.*` | slices, selections, diagnostics and statistics (@sec-ch14-schedule) | per case | the test cases |
| `test_output_barrier` | two ranks, two blocks each: on return every rank opens the combined file, which holds every global cell with its value | exact | file contents |
| `test_netcdf_utils` | variable names are sanitised to NetCDF rules | exact | string compare |

: Tests of NetCDF output. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch14-netcdf-tests}

`[C17]` of `derivation_check.py`: on $2\times10^5$ random normal-range doubles the largest relative error of the cast is
$5.948\times10^{-8}\le2^{-24}$. `[C18]`: a value above the float32 maximum becomes infinite. `[C19]`: on
$2\times10^4$ float32-exact times, a step below $2^{-25}t$ vanishes and one above $2^{-23}t$ shows.[^ch14-netcdf-chk]

[^ch14-netcdf-chk]: [sha: snapy@73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062; deck: the check itself; run:
    `python3 src/snapy_report/ch14/checks/derivation_check.py`, CPU, double, 1 process;
    Python 3.12.3, numpy 2.2.4, sympy 1.14.0; output identical to the committed file]. Output `derivation_check.out`, lines `[C17]`–`[C19]`.

The precision cases are the `OutputPrecision` tests in {{< code tests/test_user_output.cpp >}} (`yaml_double_precision_defaults_off_and_is_reported`,
`netcdf_float_output_keeps_nonfinite`, `netcdf_double_precision_reads_back_exactly`,
`netcdf_output_without_netcdf_writes_nothing`); the barrier case is `combined_output_is_complete_when_every_rank_returns`
({{< code tests/test_output_barrier.cpp Mesh.combined_output_is_complete_when_every_rank_returns >}}). All three
ctests pass at the pin (@tbl-ch14-ctest-run), and the `ch14-netcdf` card ran there.[^ch14-netcdf-card]

[^ch14-netcdf-card]: [sha: snapy@73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062; deck: `examples/straka_single.yaml` with
    `nlim: 20`; run: `./straka.release card.yaml` in `build/bin` of a CPU Release build of the pin, 1 process;
    scope: the whole run, wall time; reps: 1]. Exit 0 in 0.66 s of wall time. The run wrote one
    combined frame, `card.out0.00000.nc`, at $t=0$, with `rho` of dimensions `(time, x1, x3, x2)` in float32, `press`
    in Pa, and the `temp` and `theta` of the example's user output; the next frame, at `dt: 900`, lies beyond 20
    cycles.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The default float output hides relative changes below about $10^{-7}$. Conservation is read from the
  double-precision cycle line, not from the files.
- `include_ghost_zones` carries a FIXME: it "probably doesn't work with grids other than CCC"
  ({{< code src/output/writer_core.cpp output_range >}}).
- The root globs every `block*` part of the frame in the output directory. Parts left over from an earlier run
  with more blocks would be joined in. This is read from the code and has not been run.
- The error path of the scope guard (a throw on the root) is not covered by a test.
:::

[^rg-0a77b7001f11]: scalar — passive-scalar options
